narrative: Material PL2__M6008FBB exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.61) with a strong statistically significant upward trend over the ~12-month observation window. Lead times are variable (CV=0.78) but short (mean ~1.04 days), keeping the demand-during-lead-time sigma at 173,589 units. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-based order quantity is recommended because demand is nearly continuous (96.8% non-zero days) and the short, variable lead times make a fixed reorder-point trigger practical and cost-efficient.
warnings: High demand variability (CV=0.611) — consider dynamic safety stock
Variable lead times (CV=0.784) — monitor supplier delivery performance
Statistically significant upward demand trend — review policy quarterly

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is nearly continuous (96.8% active days) with erratic but non-intermittent variability, making a continuous-review reorder-point model appropriate. EOQ balances the relatively low ordering cost against the unit holding cost; the MOQ (24,719) is well below the EOQ (66,938) so it does not bind.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (4,490,135 units) is far above the maximum post-replenishment inventory level (352,467 units), so no capacity risk exists. The growing demand trend is the primary boundary risk — if mean demand rises materially, the reorder point will need upward revision to avoid stockouts.
